title: Horseshoe lemma with prescribed end resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives], and let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be a short exact sequence in $\mathcal A$. Let $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$ and $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$ be given injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $I_A^n=I_C^n=0$ for $n<0$. Then there exist an injective resolution $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$ with $I_B^n=0$ for $n<0$ and morphisms of complexes $\alpha:I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet$, $\beta:I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet$ such that $\alpha^0\circ s_A=s_B\circ f$, $\beta^0\circ s_B=s_C\circ g$, and for every $n\geq0$ the sequence $0\to I_A^n\xrightarrow{\alpha^n}I_B^n\xrightarrow{\beta^n}I_C^n\to0$ is short exact. (One may take $I_B^n=I_A^n\oplus I_C^n$ with $\alpha^n,\beta^n$ the inclusion and the projection.)

source.place: Lemma 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), last sentence: given injective resolutions A -> I and C -> J one can take I_1 = I and I_3 = J

proof.text: (Degree-zero step, for any short exact sequence.) Let $0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be short exact and $u:A'\to J_A$, $v:C'\to J_C$ monomorphisms into injective objects. Since $J_A$ is injective and $f'$ is a monomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions], there is $\lambda:B'\to J_A$ with $\lambda f'=u$. Put $J_B=J_A\oplus J_C$, which is injective (a morphism into a biproduct is a pair of morphisms, so extensions can be taken componentwise), $w=(\lambda,vg'):B'\to J_B$, and let $\iota:J_A\to J_B$, $\pi:J_B\to J_C$ be the inclusion and the projection. Then $\iota u=(\lambda f',vg'f')=wf'$ because $g'f'=0$, and $\pi w=vg'$; the row $0\to J_A\xrightarrow{\iota}J_B\xrightarrow{\pi}J_C\to0$ is split exact.

source.place: Lemma 013T, proof Step 2: I_2^n = I_1^n + I_3^n with the maps B^n -> I_2^n built from the outer ones

proof.text: (Kernels and cokernels.) In the situation of Step 1, apply the snake lemma [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian] to the commutative diagram with rows $0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0$ and $0\to J_A\to J_B\to J_C\to0$ and vertical maps $u,w,v$. As $\operatorname{Ker}u=\operatorname{Ker}v=0$, exactness at $\operatorname{Ker}w$ gives $\operatorname{Ker}w=0$, so $w$ is a monomorphism; the connecting map from $\operatorname{Ker}v=0$ vanishes, so $\operatorname{Coker}u\to\operatorname{Coker}w$ is a monomorphism, and $\pi$ epi makes $\operatorname{Coker}w\to\operatorname{Coker}v$ an epimorphism. Hence $0\to\operatorname{Coker}u\to\operatorname{Coker}w\to\operatorname{Coker}v\to0$ is short exact, and the quotient maps $J_X\to\operatorname{Coker}$ commute with $\iota,\pi$ and the induced maps.

source.place: Lemma 013T, proof (exactness of the constructed rows)

proof.text: (Induction with the prescribed outer terms.) Put $K_X^{-1}=X$ and $e_X^{-1}=s_X$ for $X=A,C$, and recursively $K_X^n=\operatorname{Coker}(e_X^{n-1})$ with quotient $p_X^n:I_X^n\to K_X^n$. Exactness of the prescribed augmented resolutions $0\to X\to I_X^0\to I_X^1\to\cdots$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] says exactly that $d_X^n=e_X^np_X^n$ for a monomorphism $e_X^n:K_X^n\to I_X^{n+1}$, and all $I_X^n$ are injective. Start with the given sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ and $u=s_A$, $v=s_C$: Step 1 gives $I_B^0=I_A^0\oplus I_C^0$, $s_B=w$, $\alpha^0=\iota$, $\beta^0=\pi$, and Step 2 a short exact sequence $0\to K_A^0\to K_B^0\to K_C^0\to0$ with $K_B^0=\operatorname{Coker}s_B$. Having $0\to K_A^n\to K_B^n\to K_C^n\to0$, apply Steps 1 and 2 to it with the prescribed monomorphisms $u=e_A^n$, $v=e_C^n$ into the prescribed injectives $I_A^{n+1}$, $I_C^{n+1}$: this gives $I_B^{n+1}=I_A^{n+1}\oplus I_C^{n+1}$, a monomorphism $e_B^n=w:K_B^n\to I_B^{n+1}$, $\alpha^{n+1}=\iota$, $\beta^{n+1}=\pi$, and the next short exact sequence of cokernels $K_X^{n+1}=\operatorname{Coker}e_X^n$. Set $d_B^n=e_B^np_B^n$. The outer complexes are never changed.

source.place: Lemma 013T, proof Step 2, carried out degree by degree with I_1 and I_3 the given resolutions

proof.text: (Verification.) The squares of Steps 1 and 2 give $\alpha^{n+1}e_A^n=e_B^n k^n$ and $\beta^{n+1}e_B^n=e_C^n l^n$, where $k^n,l^n$ are the maps of cokernels, and $k^np_A^n=p_B^n\alpha^n$, $l^np_B^n=p_C^n\beta^n$; hence $\alpha^{n+1}d_A^n=d_B^n\alpha^n$ and $\beta^{n+1}d_B^n=d_C^n\beta^n$, so $\alpha,\beta$ are morphisms of complexes, and the degree-zero case is $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$. Since $e_B^n$ is a monomorphism and $p_B^n$ an epimorphism, $\ker d_B^n=\ker p_B^n=\operatorname{im}e_B^{n-1}=\operatorname{im}d_B^{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, $\ker d_B^0=\operatorname{im}s_B$ and $s_B$ is a monomorphism; so $0\to B\to I_B^0\to I_B^1\to\cdots$ is exact, the $I_B^n$ are injective and zero for $n<0$, and $s_B$ is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Each row $0\to I_A^n\to I_B^n\to I_C^n\to0$ is the split sequence of inclusion and projection.

lean.statement: theorem exists_horseshoe_prescribed_resolutions {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C] (S : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) (IA : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (IC : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) : ∃ (IB : InjectiveResolution S.X₂) (α : IA.cocomplex ⟶ IB.cocomplex) (β : IB.cocomplex ⟶ IC.cocomplex), IA.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.f ≫ IB.ι ∧ IB.ι ≫ β = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.g ≫ IC.ι ∧ ∃ (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0), ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact ∧ ∃ e : IB.cocomplex.X n ≅ IA.cocomplex.X n ⊞ IC.cocomplex.X n, α.f n ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧ β.f n = e.hom ≫ biprod.snd
